tagline: Andaman limestone cliffs, white-sand beaches, clear islands, rock climbing at Railay, and emerald-green water
introHtml:
Krabi is an Andaman coast province people picture as limestone karsts rising straight out of the sea, with white sand and clear water at their feet. The best-known spot is Ao Nang, the hub for hotels and restaurants, where you hop on a longtail boat out to Railay, Phra Nang Cave, and the four-island tour all in a single day. If you'd rather have a big island to yourself, you can catch a boat to Koh Phi Phi and Koh Lanta, which both sit within the province too.

The town itself has a walking street, a morning market, and bold southern Thai food. If you don't want to stay only by the sea, climb the thousand-plus steps at Wat Tham Sua to pay respects at the summit, soak in the Emerald Pool and the hot waterfall in the Khao Phanom Bencha forest, or scale the limestone walls at Railay, a climbing spot people fly in from all over the world to try. People come to Krabi to laze on the beach, take island-hopping boats, and get into the forest.
bestTime: November–April: clear skies, calm seas, and clear water, ideal for island-hopping boats and snorkeling. Heavy monsoon rain runs May–October.

highlights.name: Ao Nang
highlights.blurb: Krabi's main beach and tourist hub, the center for hotels, restaurants, and the longtail boat pier. Stroll the beachfront in the evening, watch the sunset, and catch boats out to the islands from here.

highlights.name: Railay and Phra Nang Cave
highlights.blurb: A headland reached only by longtail boat, with white sand, limestone walls for climbing, and Phra Nang Cave where people leave offerings. It's a spot rock climbers fly in from around the world to try.

highlights.name: Four-island tour
highlights.blurb: The classic boat route out of Ao Nang to Koh Poda, Chicken Island, Phra Nang Cave, and Talay Waek, where the tide drops and you can walk across the sandbars linking the islands. It's the province's most popular day trip.

highlights.name: Koh Phi Phi and Koh Lanta
highlights.blurb: The big islands within Krabi. Koh Phi Phi has Maya Bay and clear green water for snorkeling over coral, while Koh Lanta is quieter, with long beaches and an easygoing feel that suits staying several nights.

highlights.name: Wat Tham Sua
highlights.blurb: A mountaintop temple reached by climbing over a thousand steps to pay respects at the summit, with views of Krabi town and limestone karsts in every direction. People climb it for the merit and the view without fail.

highlights.name: Emerald Pool and hot waterfall
highlights.blurb: In the Khao Phanom Bencha forest there's an emerald-green pool fed by a natural spring to soak in, plus a hot waterfall running over warm rocks. It's a forest nature spot, a change from the seaside.

foodScene.name: Andaman seafood
foodScene.note: Right on the sea with a fishing fleet, so there's fresh shrimp, shellfish, crab, fish, and blue swimmer crab. Seafood spots in town and along Ao Nang do it grilled, steamed, stir-fried with curry powder, and in tom yum.

foodScene.name: Bold southern Thai food
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, yellow curry, khua kling, and pad sataw kung, eaten with hot rice and fresh raw veggies. It's the local everyday meal you can find all over town.

foodScene.name: Khanom jeen with southern curry
foodScene.note: A popular breakfast: rice noodles with bold southern nam ya curry, eaten with all sorts of raw veggies like yardlong beans, pennywort, and cashew shoots. The khanom jeen shops open early.

foodScene.name: Southern khao yam
foodScene.note: Rice tossed with budu sauce, shredded veggies, toasted coconut, and dried shrimp, sour-salty-sweet all in one plate. It's a light meal southerners eat regularly.

foodScene.name: Roti and cha chak at Muslim shops
foodScene.note: Krabi has a large Muslim community, and roti–cha chak shops are open from morning to late night. The roti is crisp outside and soft inside, eaten with curry or drizzled with milk, with hot pulled tea on the side.

foodScene.name: Chicken curry over rice and southern rice-and-curry
foodScene.note: Rice-and-curry shops in town ladle several southern dishes over rice — chicken curry, yellow curry, and stir-fried chili — a quick lunch for working locals.

foodScene.name: Krabi morning market and walking street
foodScene.note: The morning market has local eats and fruit, while the weekend walking street has street food, traditional sweets, and grilled seafood to graze on.

foodScene.name: Coffee and cliffside cafes
foodScene.note: Around town and along Ao Nang there are laid-back cafes with views of the limestone karsts. Many brew fresh coffee from local beans, an easy spot to stop for a cup during the day.

attractions.name: Ao Nang Beach
attractions.blurb: The main beach and tourist district with hotels, restaurants, and the longtail boat pier. Stroll the beachfront, watch the sunset, and catch boats out to the islands from here.

attractions.name: Railay and Phra Nang Cave
attractions.blurb: A headland reachable only by longtail boat, with white sand, limestone walls for climbing, and the seaside Phra Nang Cave. It's a climbing spot people come from around the world to try.

attractions.name: Talay Waek and the four-island tour
attractions.blurb: At low tide a sandbar links the islands so you can walk across. Boats run from Ao Nang to Koh Poda, Chicken Island, and clear-water spots on a day trip.

attractions.name: Koh Phi Phi
attractions.blurb: Clear-water islands with Maya Bay, Pileh Lagoon, and spots for snorkeling over coral. Go by boat for a day trip or stay overnight on the island.

attractions.name: Koh Lanta
attractions.blurb: A big island with a quiet, easygoing feel, long beaches, and clear water, plus Lanta Old Town by the sea and sea-gypsy life. It suits people who want to stay several nights at a slow pace.

attractions.name: Wat Tham Sua
attractions.blurb: A mountaintop temple where you climb over a thousand steps to pay respects at the summit, with views of Krabi town and limestone karsts all around. A spot for merit-making and the view.

attractions.name: Emerald Pool and Khlong Thom hot waterfall
attractions.blurb: An emerald-green pool fed by a natural spring in the Khao Phanom Bencha forest, plus a hot waterfall running over warm rocks to soak in deep in the woods.

attractions.name: Khao Khanab Nam
attractions.blurb: Two limestone karsts flanking the Krabi River in front of town, a symbol of the province. You can kayak or take a boat to see the mangrove forest around the cliffs.

itineraryIdeas: Krabi 2D1N — Ao Nang, Railay, and the four-island tour
Krabi for nature — Emerald Pool, hot waterfall, Wat Tham Sua
Krabi for islands — Koh Phi Phi and Koh Lanta, staying overnight
Krabi for cafes and old town — walking street and Khao Khanab Nam
Krabi–Phuket — down the Andaman, two seaside towns
Krabi–Trang — islands and the Emerald Cave on the Andaman side
